name: Accelerometer, LinearAccelerationSensor, GravitySensor
plain: Reads device acceleration, with or without gravity, as a stream.
meaning: Shows how the phone moves and rests: walking cadence, vehicle vibration, on a table or in a pocket. Sensor noise can fingerprint the hardware.

web.api: new Accelerometer({frequency, referenceFrame}); new LinearAccelerationSensor(); new GravitySensor()

access.prompt_ui: Chromium shows no bubble: access follows the Motion sensors site setting (default Allow) plus the Permissions API name. Safari and Firefox do not ship the API.
access.persistence: Site setting Allow or Block per origin
access.iframe: Cross-origin iframes blocked unless allow="accelerometer"; page must be focused and visible
steps: 'reading' events fire; 'error' event on NotAllowedError or NotReadableError

data.metric: Sensor readings at the requested frequency

limits.headline: Can feel how your device moves and rests while the page is open
limits.user_action: Nothing in most browsers. Chrome allows it by default unless you changed Motion sensors in site settings
can: Measure movement with or without gravity
Spot walking, riding in a vehicle, or lying on a table
Move a game or view as you shake or tilt
cannot: Run in Firefox or Safari, which do not support it
Show a prompt in Chrome; there is none by default
Measure movement while the page is closed
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Safari and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: The page reads a live stream of how your device moves and which way is down.

marketing.name: Generic Sensor API
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes a common way for web pages to read motion and environment sensors such as accelerometer and gyroscope.

story.for_you: You shake or walk and a web app reacts, for example a step counter or a ball that rolls. On many phones there is no big prompt. Tiny differences in the sensor can also make your device recognizable.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for tilt controls, step counting and gestures. Trackers use sensor noise as a fingerprint, and researchers showed walking patterns and keystrokes can be guessed from it.

use_cases.example: A browser racing or maze game lets you steer by tilting your phone.
A web fitness page counts steps or jumps and times your reps.
A fall detection or walking test page uses motion to check balance.
A web AR scene keeps a model steady as you move your phone.
A fraud tool checks for natural motion, since a bot farm phone sits perfectly still.
A fingerprinting script uses sensor noise to recognize a phone across sites.

technical_bounds: Stops when the page is hidden

history.change: Generic Sensor API and Accelerometer ship
Mozilla and WebKit declined Generic Sensor citing fingerprinting
